user_goal: The user intentionally deleted the recurring Continuity monitors; the system must not treat their absence as an unexplained fault or silently recreate them.
counterexample: Current ChatGPT automation reread contains none of the declared core Continuity monitor tasks, while TASK_MANIFEST/HARNESS_STATUS still claim hourly/enabled monitor liveness.

parent_system_outline.live_authority: ChatGPT automation product-state reread for whether a task currently exists/is enabled
parent_system_outline.durable_policy_authority: Universal GitHub main for expected monitoring semantics and maintenance policy

history.prior_repair: peer liveness checks among three recurring monitors
history.known_limit: simultaneous loss of all monitors is not self-detectable by peer checks
history.abstraction_escalation: state-authority model rather than another peer/watchdog mechanism

inputs: user correction that deletion was intentional
learning_scout.reason: The failure is an internal authority/freshness mismatch and the decisive current product fact is directly observable from the connected automation surface; external literature cannot make a stale repository snapshot current.

alternatives.reason: Would override explicit user intent and still not solve stale repository observation semantics.

alternatives.option: replace ENABLED with DELETED as current durable truth
alternatives.reason: Another external product mutation could make that snapshot stale again.

alternatives.option: separate desired policy from last-observed product snapshot and require live reread for current liveness claims
alternatives.reason: Closes the recurring authority error without another monitor or authority surface.

verified_facts: the current product-state listing lacks the three declared core Continuity monitors
the user states they intentionally deleted the monitors
the repository still contains enabled/hourly current-state claims
user_decisions: Whether to recreate monitoring later is a future user/product choice; this repair must not infer consent.
unknowns: The historical actor that caused the earlier enabled-to-disabled transitions in issue #12 remains unresolved unless separately evidenced.

instruction_surface.reason: The startup hook already routes maintenance correctly; the defect is post-bootstrap external-state freshness, so adding prompt text would not enforce liveness freshness.

design.invariant: Repository monitor fields are policy or timestamped last-observed snapshots, never proof of current ChatGPT scheduler liveness. Any material decision that depends on current monitor existence/enabled state must reread the product surface.
patch: replace current-looking enabled/hourly monitor claims in the task manifest with external-product-state/live-reread semantics and the latest observed user-deleted snapshot
refresh HARNESS_STATUS as a rebuildable last-observed snapshot rather than current liveness attestation
refresh HANDOFF open gates and next-action semantics
add the invariant to SYSTEM_BLUEPRINT without introducing a new authority
comment on issue #12 to distinguish the current intentional deletion from the unresolved historical silent-disable incident

complexity_budget.steady_state_cost: one live product-state reread only when a decision actually depends on monitor liveness

architecture_payoff_deletion_test.payoff: prevents intentional or external scheduler mutations from leaving the control plane with false current-liveness assertions
architecture_payoff_deletion_test.deletion: removes semantic reliance on persistent enabled/hourly flags as present-tense truth

assurance_ceiling: This repair can make repository claims truthful and freshness-aware; it cannot make the ChatGPT scheduler itself observable when no product-state tool is available, nor can it prevent external deletion.
